articles.title: Joe Root scripts history, becomes first player to achieve this feat
articles.summary: Cricket News: Joe Root etched his name into the World Test Championship record books on Friday, becoming the first player to score 3,000 runs as a captain in the WT.
articles.body: Joe Root etched his name into the World Test Championship record books on Friday, becoming the first player to score 3,000 runs as a captain in the WTC during England’s opening Test against Pakistan at Headingley in Leeds.Root needed 42 runs to reach the landmark at the start of the match and completed the milestone in the second session of Day 2. The Yorkshire batter had resumed the day unbeaten on 37 after England reached 112-2 on a rain-affected opening day. He added the remaining five runs after lunch to bring up 3,000 WTC runs as captain.The 35-year-old returned to the England captaincy following Ben Stokes’ retirement from international cricket in June 2026. His latest achievement further underlined his consistency in the longest format, with Root now having 3,000 runs from 34 matches and 63 innings as WTC captain. He has scored eight centuries and 13 fifties, with a highest score of 228, while averaging 50.13.Root is comfortably ahead of the leading run-scorers in the WTC as captain. Former England skipper Stokes occupies second place with 2,182 runs from 40 matches, followed by Sri Lanka’s Dimuth Karunaratne on 2,160. West Indies captain Kraigg Brathwaite has 1,994 runs, while Pakistan’s Babar Azam has 1,918.Root’s milestone came during another strong batting display from England, who ended Day 2 on 366-8, taking a first-innings lead of 195 runs over Pakistan.Root scored 66 and played a key role in a 150-run partnership with Jordan Cox, who made 73. Harry Brook narrowly missed out on a century, falling for 91 at his home ground. Dan Lawrence, playing his first Test in two years, also contributed with a 51.Pakistan’s Ali Usman was the standout bowler, claiming 5-92 for his first five-wicket haul in Test cricket.The visitors had been dismissed for just 171 on the opening day, leaving England firmly in control of the first Test. Pakistan’s bowling and fielding also came under scrutiny as England’s batters capitalised on several opportunities to build a substantial lead.For Root, however, the focus was on another landmark in a Test career that continues to produce records. His 3,000 WTC runs as captain put him alone at the top of the tournament’s captaincy batting charts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Pakistan a poor side': Former England great delivers blunt verdict
articles.summary: Former England fast bowler Stuart Broad has delivered a blunt verdict on Pakistan, describing them as a \"poor side\" and backing England to complete a 3-0
articles.body: Former England fast bowler Stuart Broad has delivered a blunt verdict on Pakistan, describing them as a "poor side" and backing England to complete a 3-0 clean sweep in the three-Test series.Speaking on The Love for Cricket Podcast, Broad was critical of Pakistan's current Test team and suggested England should be expected to dominate the series."They are a poor side, they are not a really good side. You would imagine and you'd think that England should win 3-0. And pretty comfortably," Broad said.The former England pacer, however, acknowledged that a clean sweep cannot be taken for granted. He added that failing to win the series would represent a major disappointment for the hosts."But that isn't guaranteed. But if England don't come out with a Test match series win, it really is a huge failure," Broad said.His comments came after Pakistan endured a difficult opening two days in the first Test at Headingley in Leeds. Pakistan were bowled out for just 171 on the opening day, with England's bowlers exposing the tourists' batting problems.England then took firm control with the bat, reaching 366-8 by stumps on Day 2 to secure a 195-run first-innings lead.Joe Root and Harry Brook were among four England batters to register half-centuries. Root made 66 and shared a 150-run partnership with Jordan Cox, who scored 73, while Dan Lawrence contributed 51 on his return to Test cricket after two years.Brook, meanwhile, narrowly missed out on a century at his home ground. The world's top-ranked Test batter made 91 after surviving an early scare when he was dropped on one. He was eventually dismissed by Pakistan spinner Ali Usman, who claimed 5-92 for his first five-wicket haul in Test cricket.England maintained a brisk scoring rate of 4.46 runs per over, although the approach was less aggressive than the traditional Bazball style associated with the previous Stokes-McCullum era.Root also missed an opportunity to add another landmark century to his record. After reaching 66, England's new Test captain was trapped lbw by Khurram Shahzad and wasted a review, with the ball-tracking showing it would have hit the middle stump.At stumps, Jamie Smith was unbeaten on 16, with Jofra Archer yet to score.With England already holding a commanding position in the first Test, Broad's prediction of a 3-0 series victory will only add to the pressure on Pakistan as the visitors look to fight their way back into the contest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Losses, betting probe, corruption: BCB suspends Bangladesh Premier League after years of chaos
articles.summary: Bangladesh’s top domestic T20 tournament, the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), will not be held this year as the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) plans to
articles.body: Bangladesh’s top domestic T20 tournament, the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), will not be held this year as the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) plans to restructure the competition, board president Tamim Iqbal said on Thursday.Tamim said the tournament has been suspended because several franchises failed to follow the league’s rules and regulations."The BPL will not happen this year," Tamim told reporters.The BPL began in 2012 and is Bangladesh’s biggest domestic cricket tournament. However, it has struggled to match the success of franchise leagues in countries such as India and Australia.Tamim said the BCB has also been dealing with unpaid dues and problems related to bank guarantees. According to him, the board has lost around $3.3 million from the BPL over the past two years."The BPL is a great product and there is a lot of interest in it. If we can do it properly, the interest will increase even more," Tamim said."BCB is supposed to make a profit from franchise cricket, not a loss. So until we fix this, holding a tournament at a loss is not important," he said.Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo reported that the BCB suffered losses of nearly 400 million Bangladeshi taka ($3.27 million) during the last two BPL seasons.Tamim said he understood the disappointment among players but believes rebuilding the tournament is more important."If I was a player, I'd be disheartened too," Tamim added."But they also know that this tournament should be staged in a way that the BCB can be proud of. Are we proud of what has happened over the last few years? Perhaps not."The BPL has faced several issues in recent months. In May, the BCB suspended a player and multiple team officials over betting violations after an anti-corruption investigation into the tournament.The previous season also saw several matches rescheduled after domestic cricketers boycotted games over comments made by BCB official Nazmul Islam, who criticised players and questioned their financial value.Tamim said the BCB is committed to bringing the tournament back but will take time to fix the problems."Our intention is 1,000 percent to host BPL. But I do not want to rush. I want to do it properly; if it takes six months or 12 months, I will take that time," he added.Tamim, who was recently appointed chairman of the International Cricket Council’s new Franchise League Committee, said Bangladesh’s experience with the BPL makes the overhaul even more important."If franchise cricket does not run properly in my country, then stopping it, and rebuilding it, will be a big message for my committee," he said.Tamim made the announcement while launching the Game Development (GD) Trophy, a new tournament featuring Bangladesh’s under-17, under-19 and under-23 teams.He added that the BCB has started discussions with existing franchises and plans to complete the franchise selection process by April or May next year. The board is also open to including foreign franchises in the revamped BPL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I would not say no': CSK legend considers England batting coach role for Ashes
articles.summary: Former Australia batter Mike Hussey has said he is open to helping England with their batting during next year’s Ashes series after being approached by
articles.body: Former Australia batter Mike Hussey has said he is open to helping England with their batting during next year’s Ashes series after being approached by England head coach Stephen Fleming.Fleming took over as England’s Test coach in July after replacing fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum. Fleming and Hussey have worked together for the last 15 years with IPL franchise Chennai Super Kings.Hussey said he was not sure whether Fleming’s approach was serious, but he would not reject the idea immediately."There is a lot of different things to consider. My short answer is I would not say no to anything really," Hussey told Fox Sports News, as quoted by Reuters."I love the coaching side of the game. I love trying to help players get better whether they are Australians, English, South Africans, Pakistan ?or India or anywhere, it does not bother me."Hussey, who scored 6,235 runs in 79 Tests for Australia, was England’s batting consultant when they won the 2022 T20 World Cup. He admitted it felt unusual wearing England colours because of the rivalry between the two countries."It would feel a bit weird – definitely – coaching for England against Australia in an Ashes series, no question," Hussey added."But if that is your job and that is what you are doing you just get on with it."I don't feel as if I am coaching against a team – that’s the thing. I sort of feel as if I am coaching with a team whether it is against Australia or South Africa or some other team."I won't be rushing into a decision. I have a very close relationship with Stephen Fleming and that has an impact on it as well. The time away from family is a real thing for me. I am not in a position to say yay or nay any time soon."Hussey also backed Fleming to do well as England coach and said he expects the team to keep playing positive cricket but with more control than in the previous era."He has a very good understanding of the game," he said."Very shrewd operator who gets that balance between enjoyment and fun and relationships."He has a great chance to do well. He wants to keep the game moving forward but perhaps not as recklessly as England have been recently. He will try and be a bit smarter with it."England will host Australia in the Ashes in June, July and August next year as they try to regain the urn for the first time since 2015.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Pass on the weed': Ex-India cricketer mocks AB de Villiers over Virat Kohli- Sachin Tendulkar take
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former India fast bowler Dodda Ganesh has taken a cheeky dig at South African great AB de Villiers after he rated Virat Kohli ahead of Sachin Tendulka.
articles.body: Former India fast bowler Dodda Ganesh has taken a cheeky dig at South African great AB de Villiers after he rated Virat Kohli ahead of Sachin Tendulkar in overseas Test conditions.De Villiers recently sparked a debate by saying Kohli was a stronger batter than Tendulkar in seam-friendly and bouncy conditions. While praising Tendulkar for showing that a subcontinent batter could succeed overseas, the former South Africa batter felt Kohli took that legacy forward and raised the bar."I think of someone like Sachin Tendulkar way back, who started that trend for India. Yet, he wasn't as strong as someone like Virat Kohli, who was even better. But Sachin was the first guy to show that as a subcontinent batter, you can do well in bouncy and seaming conditions. Virat took that forward and raised the bar," he said.Ganesh did not agree with the assessment and responded to the comments on X with a cheeky one-liner."Pass on the weed, brother," he wrote.De Villiers and Kohli share a close friendship, which perhaps explains the former South Africa batter's assessment. However, Tendulkar's overseas Test numbers provide a strong counterpoint.Tendulkar scored 8,705 runs in 106 overseas Tests at an average of 54.7, including 29 centuries. Kohli has 4,894 runs in 68 overseas Tests at an average of 41.51.While Kohli has several remarkable Test achievements to his name, Tendulkar's overall record remains difficult to overlook. In every country except the West Indies, Tendulkar has a better Test record than Kohli, although the former's considerably longer career is an important factor.Tendulkar's longevity was particularly evident towards the end of his career. In the final four years of his career, he scored 2,951 runs, eight centuries and 14 fifties in 29 Tests. Kohli, in comparison, managed 1,912 runs in 36 Tests between 2020 and 2025.Kohli certainly has achievements that Tendulkar did not. He scored four centuries in the 2014-15 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, led India to their first Test series win in Australia and produced two outstanding calendar years, scoring 1,215 runs in 2016 and 1,322 in 2018. He also scored 650-plus runs in a Test series on two occasions.But Tendulkar's late-career resurgence was extraordinary. In 2010, aged 37, he scored more than 1,500 runs in 14 Tests, including seven centuries. He scored 213 runs against South Africa, 390 against Sri Lanka and 403 against Australia that year.He then continued that form into 2011, scoring 326 runs in three Tests in South Africa and completing his 50th and 51st Test centuries.Kohli's Test legacy, meanwhile, extends beyond his batting numbers. As captain, he played a major role in transforming India's approach to Test cricket and led the team to a historic series win in Australia.His peak years remain among the finest by an Indian batter. In 2018, he scored 697 runs in England, including three centuries, and also became the first Indian to score four double-centuries in a calendar year.There is little debate over Kohli's standing in white-ball cricket, where his record puts him among the very best. But when the comparison is specifically about Test cricket, de Villiers' assessment is certain to remain contentious.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'They are going to come harder': Bangladesh brace for wounded Australia in second Test
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bangladesh coach Phil Simmons expects Australia to respond strongly in the second Test after his side recorded a nine-wicket win in the series opener .
articles.body: Bangladesh coach Phil Simmons expects Australia to respond strongly in the second Test after his side recorded a nine-wicket win in the series opener in Darwin.The result was Bangladesh's first Test victory on Australian soil and was described by Australian media as the "Darwin Disaster". Simmons said his players cannot afford to relax when they face the World Test Championship leaders in Mackay from Saturday."The only thing I had to say to them - and I will repeat it anyway - is that Australia is going to come harder," Simmons said."We have to either keep that level of performance or get a little bit better. Even if we have to get 1% better in some areas, then we will have to make sure that that's there.""But we know that they are going to change their game. They are going to come harder at us."Simmons said the victory in Darwin was among the most satisfying results of his coaching career in Test cricket.Bangladesh could also retain the same XI for the second Test despite left-arm pacer Shoriful Islam pushing for a return. Shoriful, who has taken 27 wickets in 13 Tests, missed the first Test because of a hamstring injury."He offers something different. But again, we just won a test match," Simmons said."I'm one ... who hardly likes to change winning teams. So it's a possibility, but I can't really say."Australia, meanwhile, confirmed one change to their team on Friday. Matt Renshaw will open the batting in place of Jake Weatherald, who was dropped on Tuesday.Captain Pat Cummins had also considered playing four pacers by bringing in Scott Boland and leaving out spinner Nathan Lyon, but the final XI was confirmed after training.Cummins said Australia need to produce a better performance in Mackay."I think if we play really well and we lose, you feel like you need to do some soul searching," he told reporters."I certainly felt like we didn't play anywhere near our best, and they played really well and they deserved to win. So, I think it's going back to when we play well.""I think everyone's in a pretty good nick. So it's just about translating our form into actually a good result."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Definitely in the scheme of things': India refuse to panic over Kuldeep Yadav after poor Galle outing
articles.summary: Cricket News: India spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule has backed Kuldeep Yadav after his quiet outing in the first Test against Sri Lanka, saying the left-arm wris.
articles.body: India spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule has backed Kuldeep Yadav after his quiet outing in the first Test against Sri Lanka, saying the left-arm wrist spinner remains an important part of the team's plans ahead of the second Test in Colombo.Kuldeep picked up just one wicket in 25 overs across both innings in Galle, while Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar shared 14 wickets between them.Bahutule said Kuldeep's role in Galle was different because of the conditions and the nature of the Kookaburra ball."He's been bowling extremely well. It's just the situation which arose in Galle, he had to play a different role. For me, he has always been a match-winner and he definitely is in the scheme of things," Bahutule told reporters at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo.He explained that wrist spinners face a bigger challenge once the Kookaburra ball becomes soft, while finger spinners can adjust their pace and grip more easily."All the spinners are struggling with the soft ball. But for finger spinners (left-arm or off-spinners), it becomes easier. For a leg-spinner, it is that much harder because of the softness of the ball, the seam just goes down."Finger spinners, you can manipulate the fingers and bowl with the speeds you want to bowl. It is a tough proposition for a (wrist) spinner."So, I don't think one game decides on the way he is performing and the way he is approaching. So, that's all he had to adapt to and he tried his best to adapt to that role."Bahutule said Kuldeep had to keep changing his pace and trajectory as the pitch slowed down during the Test."We had to see how the trajectory or the speeds work in every session. As the days went by and as there was a demand for different types of speeds and different types of trajectories, he definitely was making an effort to bowl that."I think he was playing his role. So, he was operating as a wrist spinner in a way where obviously the wicket got slower and slower each day. But I'm sure he was bowling the way he normally bowls," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Iceman': Sunil Gavaskar compares Mohit Ulva to MS Dhoni after U19 Asia Cup final heroics
articles.summary: Legendary Indian cricketer Sunil Gavaskar has praised young batter Mohit Ulva for his match-winning performance against Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup 2026
articles.body: Legendary Indian cricketer Sunil Gavaskar has praised young batter Mohit Ulva for his match-winning performance against Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup 2026 final. Gavaskar compared Ulva's calmness under pressure to former India captain MS Dhoni after the youngster helped India pull off an incredible victory.India were chasing a target of 338 but looked almost certain to lose after slipping to 252/8.However, lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva turned the match around by scoring the runs needed in the final eight overs.Gavaskar Compares Ulva To MS DhoniComing in at No. 10, Ulva played a stunning unbeaten knock of 49 runs from just 26 balls. His innings included five fours and three sixes. With three runs needed off the final delivery, he stepped out and hit a boundary over extra cover to seal India's victory.Gavaskar was impressed by the youngster's ability to stay calm in such a tense situation and compared his finishing skills to Dhoni."He (Ulva) showed coolness like MS Dhoni. Iceman. He just came out, hit a four, and saw. The non-striker was very happy. He took his helmet off, kept it down, and then raised his hands," Gavaskar said on Sony Sports.Gavaskar Recalls Dhoni's 2011 World Cup MomentGavaskar also compared Ulva's winning shot and celebration to Dhoni's famous six that sealed India's victory in the 2011 ODI World Cup final."Had MS Dhoni been there, he would have done like that too. You have seen the way MS Dhoni raised his bat after hitting the six in the World Cup. It's memorable, and this is also memorable," Gavaskar added.He also praised the Indian youngsters for refusing to give up despite losing eight wickets while chasing a big target."The biggest thing was that they never gave up. The score was 252 when the eighth wicket fell. More than 80 runs were required for a win. However, they kept their target in front of them," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kevin Pietersen fires England up ahead of ODI cricket decider, saying 'winning in Australia is the best thing you can have'
articles.summary: Gus Atkinson says it was "nice" to see Australia fans leave early as England levelled three-match ODI series with emphatic victory at Adelaide Oval on Sunday; Atkinson took 4-28 as hosts rolled for 220; Wednesday's final fixture in Hobart (3.30am start UK time) now winner-takes-all
articles.body:
England batting great Pietersen is now a white-ball mentor with the side in a role that will run up to and including the 50-over World Cup in Africa in late 2027.

The 46-year-old will not be with the team for the winner-takes-all ODI in Tasmania, having flown to India for a YouTube conference, but gave his players some words to ponder before departing.

"KP said that winning in Australia is the best thing you can have as an England cricketer," Atkinson told reporters, with Pietersen having been part of the touring side to win the Ashes down under in 2010-11 under the captaincy of Sir Andrew Strauss.

Atkinson: Nice to see Australia fans leaving

Atkinson impressed as England levelled the ODI series in Adelaide on Sunday, bagging 4-28 as Australia were rolled for 220 chasing 356.

Three of his wickets came inside the first seven overs as the home side slumped to 29-4 during a 135-run hammering.

The Surrey quick said, after the local fans drifted away long before their team's defeat was complete, that it was nice (to see their supporters leaving).

"I said to Harry Brook at mid-off, 'listen, it's so quiet now'. It was really nice. We copped it a bit during the [2025-26] Ashes, so to come here and win was great.

England bounced back emphatically from their seven-wicket drubbing in Perth two days earlier , posting 355-6 - their highest ODI score in Australia - thanks largely to Tom Banton's 121 from 99 balls before dismissing their hosts in 44.3 overs.

Atkinson added: "The first game didn't go to plan but to come back and have the series on the line in Hobart is very exciting. If we can come away with it, that would be fantastic."

Banton's century was his sixth fifty-plus score in nine innings (two hundreds, four half-centuries) since replacing the injured Jacob Bethell at the top of the ODI batting order, during which time the Somerset man has hit 540 runs at an average of 60.

The 28-year-old said, when asked whether he felt comfortable in his spot: "I guess so, but I'm not thinking too much about it - that's for other people to do.

"I'm just trying to do as well as I can and score as many runs as I can for England. That question, and the answer, is for the people with higher power. I'm just focusing on the game."

Australia are likely to bring young pace prospect Mahli Beardman back into their XI for the Hobart decider (3.30am UK time on Wednesday).

The 21-year-old took 6-24 at Optus Stadium last week but was then rested in Adelaide, with Riley Meredith coming into the side in his place.

articles.title: Rajat Patidar scripts SMAT history, set new state record for most sixes
articles.summary: Rajat Patidar delivered a stunning batting performance in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy on Monday, smashing an unbeaten 135 off just 48 balls to help Madhya
articles.body: Rajat Patidar delivered a stunning batting performance in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy on Monday, smashing an unbeaten 135 off just 48 balls to help Madhya Pradesh post 250/6 against Assam in New Chandigarh.His innings included 13 sixes and eight fours, with his century coming in just 41 deliveries.The knock was special for several reasons, as Patidar became the first Madhya Pradesh batter to score a century in the history of the tournament.He also set a new state record for the most sixes in a single Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy innings.Patidar turns the game around with record-breaking knockPatidar came to the crease when Madhya Pradesh were struggling at 57/3 in the eighth over. However, the captain wasted little time and launched an aggressive attack on Assam's bowlers.He received excellent support from Shivang Kumar, who joined him in the middle. The duo added 153 runs from just 62 balls, recording the second-highest partnership for Madhya Pradesh in the tournament.Patidar was particularly impressive, facing only five dot balls throughout his innings.The explosive performance comes at an important time for Patidar, especially with the IPL 2027 retention deadline falling on November 17. He is an important player for Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), and his latest knock will be encouraging news for the franchise.Patidar had recently withdrawn from India's Rising Stars Asia Cup squad in Doha to manage his existing injuries. He was initially named vice-captain of the India A team but informed the BCCI that he did not wish to be considered for 50-over cricket at the time.Ayush Badoni replaced him, while Rinku Singh took over as vice-captain.Despite the fitness concerns, Patidar has started the domestic season strongly. He scored an unbeaten 36 against Keralam in Madhya Pradesh's opening Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match and also registered back-to-back centuries against Puducherry and Bihar in the Ranji Trophy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Who is this cocky little guy?':  Dale Steyn's first impression of young Virat Kohli
articles.summary: Former South African fast bowler Dale Steyn has recalled his first impression of a young Virat Kohli, admitting that the Indian batting star initially
articles.body: Former South African fast bowler Dale Steyn has recalled his first impression of a young Virat Kohli, admitting that the Indian batting star initially struck him as a rather cocky youngster during the 2008 Under-19 World Cup. However, their subsequent association at Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) brought the two closer, with a shared love for food and music helping them develop a strong off-field bond.Steyn was speaking alongside former South African captain Faf du Plessis on ESPNcricinfo's show 'Cricketers on Cricketers', where he looked back at his early interactions with Kohli and the Indian's transformation into one of the biggest names in world cricket.The former pacer, who represented RCB during the first three IPL seasons from 2008 to 2010, recalled watching India defeat South Africa in the Under-19 World Cup final in 2008. Kohli had captained India to the title, and Steyn, who had been following the tournament, was left with a rather strong first impression of the youngster."I actually remember watching the Under-19 World Cup. We had a tour of India. Sehwag had just smashed us. He scored 300 in Chennai in a day (in 2008). We had had a tour somewhere else, maybe just before that. I think we had even gone to Bangladesh just before that. I remember watching India beat South Africa U-19s in the [2008] World Cup, and India stormed the field. And I saw this kid, and I was like, who's this cocky little bloody s***? You know? And the next thing I find out, he's actually in my team," Steyn said.The South African admitted that he initially wondered how he would deal with the youngster when they became teammates at RCB. However, his perception changed once they got to know each other, as the two discovered several common interests away from cricket."He is with us at RCB. And I'm like, oh my goodness. I gotta deal with this little guy, you know? Anyway, it turns out when I met him, we had a lot of common interests. We were young, and we enjoyed a little bit of an off-the-field kind of enjoyment in life. We used to go to all the restaurants and stuff that Bangalore had to offer - Hard Rock Cafe was a particular favourite. There was good music and there were burgers and everything like that. So, we hung out quite a lot," he recalled.Steyn also offered an interesting glimpse into Kohli's early days, describing him as a relatively laid-back youngster before commercial success and endorsements began changing his public image. While he recognised the Indian's natural ability, he felt the batter still needed some guidance at that stage of his career."In the early days of Virat Kohli, he was a normal T-shirt and shorts with the slops [flip-flops] kind of guy. Then the sponsors rolled in. You could tell, from a cricketing point of view, he was talented, but he needed a little bit of direction," Steyn added.Kohli's journey in the league, however, did not begin with such extraordinary numbers. Across his first three IPL seasons, Kohli accumulated 718 runs in 45 matches at an average of 21.75, registering just two half-centuries.He has since gone on to become the IPL's leading run-scorer, with 9,336 runs in 283 matches, including nine hundreds and 68 fifties. Between 2023 and 2026, he enjoyed another prolific phase, becoming the first batter in IPL history to register four consecutive seasons with more than 600 runs. Two of those campaigns also contributed to RCB's back-to-back title triumphs.At the international level, Kohli has crossed 28,000 runs and scored 86 centuries. He has also won all three major white-ball ICC titles - the ODI World Cup, T20 World Cup and Champions Trophy - besides collecting individual honours, including Player of the Tournament awards at World Cups in both formats and multiple Player of the Match awards in ICC events.Kohli's latest assignment was India's ODI series in New Zealand, where he scored 86 runs in four innings, including a half-century. He is expected to return to action against Sri Lanka in a three-match ODI series beginning December 13.In 14 ODIs and 13 innings this year, the former India captain has scored 638 runs at an average of 53.17 and a strike rate of over 118, with two centuries and four half-centuries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Litton Das gave his daughter Anayra a birthday present to cherish, celebrating her special day with a magnificent century against South Africa in the first Test at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. Unable to be with his little princess on her birthday, the Bangladesh batter found a special way to make the occasion memorable, dedicating his eighth Test hundred to her with a handwritten message that brought a personal touch to his fighting knock.After reaching the three-figure mark on the second morning, Das pulled out a handwritten note from his pocket and held it up for the cameras. The message read: "Happy Birthday to my Princess. This 100 is for you!"It was an emotional moment for the Bangladesh batter, who had already expressed his love for his daughter through a heartfelt social media post ahead of the occasion."Happy Birthday, my princess! I wish I could be with you on your special day, but even from afar, you are always in my thoughts and prayers. My blessings are with you, today and always. May you always be blessed with good health, happiness, and a beautiful heart. Grow up to be a wonderful person and keep shining, my little one. Your dad loves you more than words can ever express."The century was particularly special as Das had to overcome a difficult situation to put Bangladesh in a commanding position after their top order had collapsed on the opening day.Litton, Hridoy script remarkable Bangladesh recoveryBangladesh were in deep trouble after opting to bat, with Kagiso Rabada ripping through their top order to reduce the visitors to 22/3 inside nine overs.The South African fast bowler dismissed debutant Mahfijul Islam, Mominul Haque and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto to put the hosts firmly in control.Towhid Hridoy and Tanzid Hasan then attempted to stabilise the innings with a 99-run partnership. Tanzid contributed 67 off 108 balls before Rabada struck again, removing him and Mushfiqur Rahim in quick succession. Bangladesh were 121/5 when Das joined Hridoy.What followed was a magnificent counterattack. The two batters stitched together a 206-run partnership for the sixth wicket, completely changing the complexion of the innings.Hridoy continued his impressive run in Test cricket, scoring 137 off 227 deliveries for his second century in just seven innings. He had struck a remarkable 224 against the West Indies recently.Das, meanwhile, brought up his half-century off 71 balls and finished the opening day unbeaten on 92. He needed only a few overs on Monday to complete his eighth Test century, becoming just the third Bangladesh batter to score a Test hundred against South Africa.He eventually departed for 120 off 179 balls, an innings featuring 14 fours and a six, after pulling Dane Paterson towards mid-wicket, where Marco Jansen completed the catch.Paterson leads South Africa's fightbackDespite the resistance from Das and Hridoy, South Africa managed to bowl Bangladesh out for 400 before lunch on the second day.Paterson was the pick of the bowlers, claiming four wickets for 92 runs, while Rabada finished with five for 51. Jansen chipped in with two wickets.South Africa began their reply cautiously but suffered an early setback when Aiden Markram was caught behind off Hasan Mahmoud for four. The hosts were 18/1 at lunch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jay Shah gets second term as ICC Chair! BCCI hails leadership as cricket prepares for Olympic return
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Monday congratulated Jay Shah on his unopposed reappointment as International Cricket
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Monday congratulated Jay Shah on his unopposed reappointment as International Cricket Council (ICC) Chair for a second term, describing the decision as a strong endorsement of his leadership as cricket prepares for a significant phase of global expansion, including its return to the Olympics at Los Angeles 2028.The ICC Board confirmed Shah's reappointment following a proposal by its directors at the Board meetings in Bali, Indonesia. Having taken charge in December 2024, Shah will continue to lead the global governing body as the sport prepares for its Olympic comeback after 128 years, with both men's and women's T20 competitions featuring in the LA28 programme.The BCCI's congratulatory message was accompanied by praise from its top officials, including president Mithun Manhas, vice-president Rajeev Shukla, secretary Devajit Saikia, joint secretary Prabhtej Bhatia, treasurer A. Raghuram Bhat and IPL chairman Arun Singh Dhumal.Shah's reappointment comes after his tenure as BCCI Honorary Secretary from 2019 to 2024, during which Indian cricket witnessed several major developments, including the launch of the Women's Premier League (WPL), pay parity in international match fees for contracted women cricketers, the Test Cricket Incentive Scheme for senior men's players and increased prize money across domestic competitions.India also hosted the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 during his tenure, which became the most attended cricket tournament in history.Congratulating Shah, BCCI president Mithun Manhas said, “I congratulate Jay Shah on being reappointed, unopposed, as ICC Chair. He worked at every level of Indian cricket before taking on the global role, and that grounding shows in how he leads. His years at the BCCI saw the game strengthened from the grassroots to the elite level, and he has brought the same outlook to the ICC. The Board’s decision, at a time of such change for the sport, reflects the confidence ICC members have in him. The BCCI wishes him well for the term ahead and stands ready to support the ICC in its work.”LA28 Olympics, global expansion on Jay Shah's agendaOne of the biggest milestones awaiting Shah during his second term will be cricket's return to the Olympic Games at Los Angeles 2028. The sport last featured at the Olympics in 1900, and its inclusion in the LA28 programme marks a significant opportunity to reach new audiences and expand its global footprint.Shah played a key role as part of the ICC's Olympics Working Group in securing cricket's inclusion in the programme. The men's and women's T20 competitions are expected to provide the sport with a major international platform beyond its traditional markets.BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla highlighted the significance of the Olympic opportunity while congratulating Shah.“It is a proud moment for Indian cricket. Jay Shah’s second term as ICC Chair comes as the game prepares to return to the Olympics at LA28, which could introduce cricket to audiences it has never reached. Indian cricket has contributed a great deal to the world game, through its players, its administrators and its passionate supporters, and it is gratifying to see that contribution recognised once again. The coming years will call for patience and careful planning, and I am confident the game is in capable hands. My best wishes to him,” Shukla said.During Shah's first term, international cricket also witnessed several major events, including the return of the ICC Men's Champions Trophy in 2025 after an eight-year gap, the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2025 and the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026, co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said Shah's unopposed reappointment reflected the confidence of the ICC Board, particularly with regard to expanding the game and creating more opportunities for emerging cricket nations.“An unopposed reappointment is a strong endorsement from the ICC Board, and Jay Shah has earned it. During his first term, the ICC has taken important steps to expand the global calendar and strengthen development and qualification pathways, creating greater opportunities for Associate Members and emerging cricket nations. The Board has also reaffirmed its commitment to the women’s game, which is welcome news for players in India and elsewhere. Cricket is now heading back to the Olympics, and it is great to see him leading the game into that chapter. We are delighted that he will continue, and on behalf of the BCCI, I wish him every success,” Saikia said.BCCI officials hail his contribution to Indian cricketBCCI joint secretary Prabhtej Bhatia pointed to the structural changes introduced during Shah's time at the Indian board, particularly those aimed at strengthening women's cricket and improving financial support for players.“My warm congratulations to Jay Shah on his reappointment as ICC Chair for a second term. What distinguishes his leadership is that he builds structures that last. At the BCCI, the WPL gave women’s cricket a professional platform, while equal international match fees and higher domestic prize money backed the players who sustain the game at every level. At the ICC, the focus on expanding the women’s game and creating more opportunities through global competitions has continued. With cricket returning to the Olympics at LA28, the foundations are now in place for the game to grow in markets where it is still new. I wish him every success in the years ahead,” Bhatia said.BCCI treasurer A. Raghuram Bhat also highlighted the importance of investment in infrastructure and domestic cricket.“Many congratulations to Jay Shah. Throughout his time at the BCCI, the emphasis was on investing in the game’s foundations, from better facilities such as the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru to stronger support for domestic cricket and its players. The ICC has set out a commitment to sustainable commercial growth, and that kind of disciplined planning will matter as the game expands. I wish him the very best.”IPL chairman Arun Singh Dhumal, who worked closely with Shah during his BCCI tenure, recalled his contribution to the commercial growth of Indian cricket, including the IPL's record media rights deal.“I worked closely with Jay Shah during his years at the BCCI, and I saw how seriously he approached the game’s commercial and competitive growth, including the IPL’s record media rights deal. He combined ambition with close attention to detail, and he was always open to new ideas that could benefit players and fans alike. Leagues like the IPL and the WPL have shown how a strong competition can lift an entire ecosystem. I congratulate him on his reappointment and wish him continued success,” Dhumal said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'He will regret it after 10 years': Kapil Dev questions Virat Kohli's big decision
articles.summary: Former India captain Kapil Dev has strongly criticised Virat Kohli's decision to retire from Test cricket, describing it as the biggest mistake of the
articles.body: Former India captain Kapil Dev has strongly criticised Virat Kohli's decision to retire from Test cricket, describing it as the biggest mistake of the batting great's career. The legendary all-rounder believes Kohli had plenty left to offer in the longest format, particularly given his exceptional fitness, and feels the 36-year-old could regret walking away from Tests in the years to come.Kohli announced his retirement from Test cricket on May 12, 2025, bringing the curtain down on a career spanning 123 matches. His final appearance in the format came against Australia in Sydney on January 3, 2025. He finished with 9,230 runs at an average of 46.85.Kapil, however, is not convinced that Kohli needed to call time on his Test career. In an interview with Mid-Day, the former India skipper questioned the timing of the decision and suggested that Kohli's physical conditioning should have allowed him to continue playing at the highest level."I think Virat Kohli made the biggest mistake. He retired from Test cricket. He will regret his decision after 10 years. He should not have retired. Kohli has fitness on his side, and his fitness is far better than any other player," Dev said.The 1983 World Cup-winning captain argued that Kohli's fitness gave him an advantage even over much younger cricketers. He also felt that players should respond to difficult phases by fighting their way back into the team rather than choosing retirement."He can challenge even a 25-year-old cricketer on fitness. Getting angry and retiring is not right. They should be like Mohinder Amarnath. He was dropped so many times, but he came back and proved others wrong," Kapil added.By bringing up Mohinder Amarnath's career, Kapil highlighted the importance of perseverance and making a comeback after setbacks. Amarnath experienced several exclusions from the Indian team but repeatedly returned to establish himself, something Kapil believes Kohli could also have attempted instead of walking away from Test cricket.Kohli's Test retirement came after he had already stepped away from T20 Internationals in 2024, following India's T20 World Cup triumph. With his departure from the longest format, the former India captain is now active only in ODI cricket at the international level.Despite moving away from two formats, Kohli continues to remain a key figure in India's 50-over plans. He is scheduled to return to action in the three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka, beginning December 13.The right-hander has enjoyed a productive run in ODIs this year. In 14 matches and 13 innings, he has accumulated 638 runs at an average of 53.17 and a strike rate of over 118. His tally includes two centuries and four half-centuries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 82 off 29 after 60 off 21! Suryakumar Yadav makes another strong statement in SMAT
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Suryakumar Yadav is making his intentions clear with the bat.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Suryakumar Yadav is making his intentions clear with the bat. The T20 World Cup-winning captain continued his stunning run in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, smashing a blistering 29-ball 82 to power Mumbai to a commanding five-wicket victory over Gujarat on Monday.It was his second consecutive fifty-plus score in the domestic T20 tournament, following his explosive 21-ball 60 against Hyderabad in Mumbai's opening match on November 14. The 36-year-old's latest assault featured nine fours and seven sixes as Mumbai chased down Gujarat's 198-run target in just 15.4 overs.Sarfaraz Khan provided the finishing support with an unbeaten 40 off 17 balls, ensuring Mumbai completed a dominant chase. Earlier, Shardul Thakur and Atharva Ankolekar had claimed three wickets apiece to restrict Gujarat, although Ashutosh Sharma (42 off 22) and Vishal Jayswal (38 off 21) lifted them to 197 with a late flourish.For Suryakumar, however, the runs carry significance beyond Mumbai's campaign. Having lost his place in the Indian side after leading the country to a second consecutive T20 World Cup title, the batter is determined to earn his way back.'I will have to break the door down once more'After his innings against Hyderabad in the SMAT opener, Suryakumar spoke candidly about the disappointment of being left out of the Indian squad and his renewed motivation to represent the country."After winning the World Cup, you naturally expect that you will play after the IPL or whenever India's first series takes place. Because you have won a major tournament, and winning an ICC event is not easy, especially on home soil, something nobody had achieved before," he said."But the selectors must have had their reasons and must have thought things through before taking that decision. But yes, I was hurt. If you don't feel sad or hurt, how will you turn that into passion, and how will you play with that passion? That is what I am trying to do now," he added.The former India T20I captain said the hunger to play for the country had returned and that he was ready to work his way back into the side."The same hunger I had earlier to play for India, when I used to score runs after returning to domestic cricket, has come back again. If I want to play for India again, I will have to break the door down once more. All right, let's do it," he said.His appointment as Mumbai captain has also given him an opportunity to lead from the front. Suryakumar expressed gratitude to Mumbai Cricket Association president Ajinkya Naik for backing him during a difficult phase and entrusting him with the responsibility."He could have chosen someone else. He had that option, but the responsibility, love and respect he has given me mean a lot. I will always remain grateful and humble for that," he said.'Not about making a statement'Suryakumar also spoke about adapting to the changing demands of T20 cricket, with teams increasingly targeting totals of 250 and beyond. He stressed the need to sustain an attacking approach through the middle overs rather than allowing the scoring rate to dip after the powerplay."After that, when we bat between overs seven and 15, it is important to maintain the same intensity and intent, even when playing for India. If we have to score 250-260, then that is what we have to do, and I am trying to follow that approach," he said."The 'high-risk, high-reward' game in the middle overs has always been part of my batting. But now I am trying to understand how I can take even more risks and hit more boundaries and sixes because T20 cricket has become a format dominated by boundaries and sixes," he added.Asked whether his innings against Hyderabad was intended as a message to the selectors, Suryakumar insisted that his focus was on enjoying his batting, scoring consistently and helping Mumbai win."It is not about making a statement. I have been batting this way for the last four or five years, and I am enjoying it just as much today. This is an entertainment format, so I want to go out there and express myself freely," he had said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why Vaibhav Sooryavanshi missed Bihar's second SMAT match after historic captaincy debut
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's stint as Bihar captain in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 lasted just one match, despite being named to lead
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's stint as Bihar captain in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 lasted just one match, despite being named to lead the side for its opening two fixtures. The 15-year-old missed Bihar's second Group B match against Railways on Monday because he was scheduled to join the India A squad for the ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 in Doha.Sooryavanshi's captaincy appointment was always intended to be a short-term arrangement. He was named Bihar captain for the first two matches against Saurashtra and Railways while regular skipper Sakibul Gani was unavailable. However, his national commitments meant he had to link up with India A ahead of the tournament, which begins on November 19.With Sooryavanshi away, Suraj Kashyap took over the leadership responsibilities for Bihar against Railways. The change did little to affect the team's performance as Bihar registered a four-wicket victory, completing their chase of 138 with 10 balls to spare.From record-breaking captaincy to India A call-upSooryavanshi made history in Bihar's tournament opener against Saurashtra on Saturday, becoming the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket at 15 years and 232 days.He surpassed Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who had previously held the record after captaining his national side at 17 years and 311 days.His captaincy debut also produced a light-hearted moment at the toss. After winning it and opting to bat, Sooryavanshi was asked about Bihar's playing XI but appeared to forget the details."I think, sir, bhool gaya lagta main (I think, sir, I have forgotten)," he said with a smile.The teenager had described the opportunity to lead his home state as a dream come true, having started his cricketing journey in Bihar. However, his first match as captain ended in defeat. He scored 18 off 12 balls before being caught and bowled by Chetan Sakariya, as Bihar managed 137/9. Saurashtra chased down the target to win the contest.Sooryavanshi's next assignment is with India A, who will be led by Tilak Varma in the Rising Stars Asia Cup. The squad also features senior India opener Abhishek Sharma, Rinku Singh, Harshit Rana and several other established domestic performers.India A are in Group B alongside Pakistan A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates. They begin their campaign against Nepal on November 20, followed by the much-anticipated clash against Pakistan A on November 22.Bihar win without their teenage captainBihar showed they could manage without their record-breaking young captain, beating Railways by four wickets in Indore.After being put in to bat, Railways were restricted to 137/9 in 20 overs. Jayant Lakhan top-scored with 47, while Zubair Ali Khan contributed 26. Prashant Singh led the bowling effort with 3/28, while Kashyap also picked up three wickets for 29 runs. Mohammed Izhar claimed two.In reply, Ayush Loharuka provided Bihar with a flying start, smashing 58 off just 29 balls, including five fours and five sixes. His dismissal at 78/2 in 8.2 overs briefly slowed the chase, but contributions from Tarun Kumar (20), Raghuvendra Pratap Singh (18) and Altamish Ashraf (15) kept Bihar on course.Kashyap remained unbeaten on 13 as Bihar reached 141/6 in 18.2 overs. His all-round contribution earned him the Player of the Match award.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli endured contrasting yet underwhelming campaigns with the bat during India's five-match ODI series against New Zealand in
articles.body: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli endured contrasting yet underwhelming campaigns with the bat during India's five-match ODI series against New Zealand in November 2026. While Rohit managed just 30 runs in four innings, failing to get off the mark twice, Kohli started the tour on a promising note with a 51-ball 74 but could not maintain the momentum.Kohli eventually ended the series with 86 runs from four innings. Despite the modest tally, the former India captain emerged as the team's leading run-scorer in the series, which India won 3-1 on Sunday. He was also the only Indian batter to register a half-century or better during the contest.The focus will now shift to Sri Lanka, with India scheduled to host the 1996 World Cup champions for a white-ball series in December. The tour comprises three ODIs and five T20Is, with Rohit and Kohli expected to return to action in the opening ODI on December 13.The first match will be held at the ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam, followed by the second ODI at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru on December 16. His highest individual score in the format, an extraordinary 264, also came against the same opposition at Eden Gardens in Kolkata.Across 55 ODIs and 53 innings against Sri Lanka, Rohit has accumulated 2,021 runs at an average of 45.93 and a strike rate of 96.97. His tally includes six centuries and nine half-centuries.Kohli's numbers against Sri Lanka are even more imposing. The former India captain has scored 2,652 runs in 54 innings across 56 ODIs, averaging 60.27 at a strike rate of 93.67. articles.title: 'He makes the ball speak': Auqib Nabi wins India's Impact Player award after New Zealand ODI series triumph
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Auqib Nabi's impressive comeback on the international stage received a special recognition after India clinched a 3-1 ODI series victory over
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Auqib Nabi's impressive comeback on the international stage received a special recognition after India clinched a 3-1 ODI series victory over New Zealand away from home. The Jammu and Kashmir pacer was named India's 'Impact Player of the Series', capping a promising campaign in which he played a key role in the visitors' bowling dominance.Nabi received the medal from India's team physiotherapist Thulasi Ram Yuvaraj inside the dressing room, with the latter praising the fast bowler's work ethic and understated personality."This person whom I am going to give this medal, I know him for some time. He is a hardworking, committed, very meticulous in his preparations. He speaks very less. He makes sure his ball speaks in the field. So, it is none other than Auqib," said Thulasi in a video posted by the BCCI on Monday.The physio also acknowledged how difficult it was to single out one player after a series in which several members of the Indian side delivered impressive performances."Congrats everyone. It was an exciting match and what an amazing series we have witnessed. I am very sure it is very difficult for whoever has made this decision because each and everyone in the team has outperformed in various aspects of this game," he added.Nabi, meanwhile, expressed gratitude for the recognition and underlined the importance of the team's series victory."Thank you for this. I am very grateful for this. I am very happy that we have won the series and I have made a contribution in it. Thank you," he said.From difficult debut to a rewarding New Zealand tourThe award marks a significant turnaround for Nabi, whose international career had a difficult start. On his ODI debut against the West Indies in Guwahati, he conceded 84 runs in 8.5 overs without taking a wicket. In New Zealand, however, the 30-year-old showed greater control and made important breakthroughs in challenging conditions.After going wicketless in the opening ODI with an economical spell of 0/33 in six overs, Nabi struck in the second match, dismissing Tim Seifert and Will Young to finish with 2/31 in seven overs. He picked up two more wickets in the fourth ODI, removing Dean Foxcroft and Kristian Clarke, before claiming the crucial wicket of Michael Bracewell in the series finale.He finished the campaign with five wickets from 31 overs at an average of 32 and an economy rate of 5.16. His best figures were 2/31.Nabi was part of an Indian pace attack that also featured Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Mohammed Siraj. The bowlers repeatedly troubled New Zealand's batters, with Arshdeep and Nabi making important contributions in the final ODI.India defended a modest 209 at Mount Maunganui, bowling New Zealand out for 187 in 48.1 overs to seal a 22-run victory. Arshdeep led the attack with 3/30, while Siraj claimed two wickets. Nabi finished with 1/37 from his 10 overs, dismissing the dangerous Bracewell.Nabi will remain in New Zealand alongside Arshdeep as India prepare for the two-Test series, beginning in Wellington on November 19. The second Test will be played in Christchurch from November 27.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen leaves England camp midway through Australia tour, heads to India; Here's why
articles.summary: England will be without the services of consultant coach Kevin Pietersen for the final leg of their white-ball tour of Australia, with the former captain
articles.body: England will be without the services of consultant coach Kevin Pietersen for the final leg of their white-ball tour of Australia, with the former captain heading to Mumbai to fulfil professional commitments. His departure comes with the three-match ODI series delicately poised at 1-1 and the decider scheduled to be played in Hobart on Wednesday under lights.Pietersen confirmed his departure through a social media post on Monday, bidding farewell to Australia after spending time with the England squad.“See ya, Aus! Thank you for the most wonderful time in your beautiful country! It’s been so good being here again, and I cannot wait to come back soon! I will say one thing — being back as a non-player is way easier than as a player. And on sandpaper - my view is — I don’t have a view! Time to get back to my day job — @kptheswitch and filming in India!” wrote Pietersen on his Instagram account on Monday.According to a report in The Telegraph, Pietersen is travelling to Mumbai to address a YouTube summit as part of his content creation commitments. His YouTube channel, ‘The Switch’, currently has 829,000 followers.The 46-year-old became part of Brendon McCullum's support staff this summer, taking up the role of specialist mentor. With Marcus Trescothick now working exclusively with England's Test team, Pietersen has effectively been involved in overseeing the batting department of the white-ball sides.Although he was present during England's home white-ball series against Australia, Pietersen did not travel with the team for last month's tri-series in Pakistan. He is expected to rejoin the squad for the three-match ODI tour of South Africa in January, which will be a significant part of England's preparations for the 2027 Men's ODI World Cup.Meanwhile, England fast bowler Gus Atkinson revealed the message Pietersen delivered to the players before leaving the camp. Atkinson, who claimed career-best figures of four for 28 in Sunday's comprehensive victory in Adelaide, said the former captain had highlighted the importance of securing a series win in Australia.“KP said that winning in Australia is the best thing as an English cricketer, so if we could come away with a series win that would be fantastic.“It was nice (to see their supporters leaving). I said to Harry Brook at mid-off: ‘Listen…it’s so quiet now.’ It was really nice. We copped it a bit during the Ashes, so coming here and winning was great. The first game didn’t go to plan, but to come back and have the series on the line in Hobart is very exciting. If we can come away with it, that would be fantastic,” Atkinson was quoted as saying by The Telegraph.England will now look to carry the momentum from their Adelaide triumph into Wednesday's series decider in Hobart, with the opportunity to finish the Australian leg on a winning note.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Russell, Pollard, Billings and Curran headline six wildcard picks for ILT20 Season 5
articles.summary: The six International League T20 (ILT20) franchises have strengthened their squads for Season 5, with Andre Russell, Tom Curran, Sam Billings, Akeal
articles.body: The six International League T20 (ILT20) franchises have strengthened their squads for Season 5, with Andre Russell, Tom Curran, Sam Billings, Akeal Hosein, Kieron Pollard and Tim Seifert joining as wildcard picks.Abu Dhabi Knight Riders have brought back Russell, defending champions Desert Vipers have signed Curran, Dubai Capitals have added Billings, Gulf Giants have picked Hosein, MI Emirates have named Pollard and Sharjah Warriorz have signed Seifert.The fifth season begins on Saturday, November 21, with Desert Vipers taking on MI Emirates in the opening match in Dubai.Russell, Curran and Billings bring proven ILT20 pedigreeRussell returns to Abu Dhabi Knight Riders, the only franchise he has represented in the ILT20, with 38 appearances. The West Indies all-rounder made history in Season 4 when his 500th T20 wicket, against Desert Vipers, made him the first player to reach 5,000 runs, 500 wickets and 500 sixes in the format.Curran is familiar with the Vipers setup, having represented them in the inaugural season when they reached the final. He also played for Gulf Giants in Season 2. Across both campaigns, the England all-rounder has scored 307 runs and taken 14 wickets in 16 appearances.Billings returns to Dubai Capitals, whom he captained to their maiden ILT20 title in Season 3. The England wicketkeeper-batter featured in the final in each of the league's first three seasons and will captain the Capitals again. He has scored 649 runs at an average of 30.90 in 29 appearances.Hosein, Pollard and Seifert add further firepowerHosein joins Gulf Giants after representing Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and MI Emirates. The West Indies left-arm spinner has taken 21 wickets in 29 appearances, with best figures of 4/23. articles.body: New Delhi: In what could be another major development before next month’s IPL auctions, Lucknow Super Giants are likely to trade Mohammed Shami to Rajasthan Royals in exchange for Sam Curran. TOI has learnt that talks are on between LSG and RR at an advanced stage. It is also learnt that RR have sought left-arm spinner M Siddharth from LSG.Shami, who recently retired from Test cricket, was traded to LSG from Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) last year for Rs 10 crore. Royals had bought Curran for Rs 2.4 crore in last year auctions before he missed the entire season due to injury.Royals head coach Kumar Sangakkara had expressed his concerns when Curran turned up to play for Surrey during a domestic T20 tournament after having ruled himself out for the entire IPL season.Curran has been close to LSG director of cricket Tom Moody. LSG’s fast bowling pool already has the likes of Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav and Mohsin Khan. LSG are looking to balance their playing XI through an allrounder albeit their batting is already heavily dependent on overseas batters like Mitchell Marsh, Aiden Markram and Nicholas Pooran.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan's WTC revival needs a major rethink! Bowling coach Shaun Tait hints at the way forward
articles.summary: Pakistan fast bowling coach Shaun Tait believes a significant change in the country's home conditions could hold the key to making the side more
articles.body: Pakistan fast bowling coach Shaun Tait believes a significant change in the country's home conditions could hold the key to making the side more competitive in the World Test Championship (WTC) in the coming years.Tait has backed the preparation of seamer-friendly pitches in Pakistan, arguing that such surfaces could help the team build a stronger fast-bowling attack and improve its prospects in the longest format.“These sort of (greenish) wickets going forward for Pakistan cricket, I believe personally is the way forward,” Tait told reporters on Monday after overseeing the fast bowlers during the final two-hour net session ahead of Tuesday's second Test against Sri Lanka.Pakistan drew the opening Test at Rawalpindi after rain and bad light resulted in at least 141 overs being lost. The match was played on a grassy surface, where 31-year-old pacer Saqib Khan made an impressive debut, claiming seven wickets.Pakistan have prepared another greenish pitch for the second Test, which was shifted from Lahore to Rawalpindi after smog levels increased in the provincial capital.“It looks similar to the last (test) pitch,” Tait said. “But again, like with the grass lengths and stuff, I’m not good with that sort of thing, but it looks like there’s some grass coverage, which is always a good sign.”Saqib's breakthrough offers Pakistan encouragementSaqib was the standout performer in the opening Test, taking 7/130 in Sri Lanka's first innings to restrict their lead to just 12 runs. His spell came under favourable overcast conditions after Kusal Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva had dominated the third day with a 249-run partnership.The fast bowler had already taken 81 wickets in 19 first-class matches over the previous four domestic seasons before earning his Test opportunity. Tait was particularly impressed by his ability to use the new ball.“He (Saqib) did a really good job, especially with the new ball,” Tait said. “Obviously he’s played quite a bit of first-class cricket, which is great … he’s got experience behind him in Pakistan, so that was really helpful to be able to bring in a player that had played enough first-class cricket and taken wickets.”Saqib was among four successful Pakistan debutants in the first Test, with Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha and Arafat Minhas scoring half-centuries.Pakistan looking to rebuild after difficult WTC campaignPakistan entered the Sri Lanka series at the bottom of the WTC standings after winning only two and losing seven Tests in the cycle.Babar Azam continued his search for a first Test century since December 2022, with his drought extending to 42 innings. Saud Shakeel also narrowly missed a century in both innings, scoring 97 in the second to help Pakistan hold on for the draw.With another green surface prepared in Rawalpindi, Pakistan will hope their fast bowlers can again make an impact as they look to build a more competitive Test side.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Sitaram, Sitaram’ from the dugout! Aaryavir Sehwag, Lakshya Raichandani relive the nerve-wracking India-Pakistan U19 Asia Cup final
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Under-19 Asia Cup triumph over Pakistan was sealed only in the final moments of a gripping contest, but for the youngsters who
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Under-19 Asia Cup triumph over Pakistan was sealed only in the final moments of a gripping contest, but for the youngsters who experienced the pressure first-hand, the memories of that nerve-wracking evening will last much longer. From Aaryavir Sehwag battling a swollen arm to keep his team in the hunt to captain Lakshya Raichandani trying to stay composed amid the tension, the two heroes have offered a glimpse into the emotions that accompanied India's thrilling title-winning chase.In a video shared by the BCCI, Sehwag and Raichandani looked back at the dramatic final in Oman, where India chased down Pakistan's imposing 338-run target with a last-ball boundary from Mohit Ulva. Sehwag revealed how he chose to continue batting despite considerable pain after being struck on the arm, while also recalling how chanting 'Sitaram, Sitaram' from the dugout helped him remain calm as the match headed towards a tense finish.‘I might not get the chance for India-Pakistan again’Sehwag, who scored 58 off 61 balls, said his arm had gone numb after being hit and that the swelling was significant. However, the thought of potentially not getting another opportunity to play Pakistan in such a high-profile final pushed him to fight through the pain."When I got hit on the arm, my arm went numb and it was really paining, it was really paining a lot. And when Suresh sir came, and he saw the swelling, he told me that, you know, it's a lot of swelling. And then I was just thinking that I might not get the chance for India-Pakistan again, and definitely not in the final, the last Under-19 India event, and I could not leave India, my team like this, and I had to fight it out. And I am grateful to God that I got the power and courage to fight through that pain there, and contribute to the team, and it was amazing," Sehwag junior said.The opener's contribution proved crucial as India made a strong start to the chase before Pakistan fought back to put the result in doubt. Sehwag also revealed that he began chanting 'Sitaram, Sitaram' from the 32nd over, drawing comfort from the belief that India could still get over the line."I had noticed Lakshya also. I don't know which name he was chanting, but I was chanting "Sitaram Sitaram" from the 32nd over. So I was chanting it from the 32nd over, and obviously there was belief in the team, and quite a lot, you know, everyone was sitting in one place, not moving from their place. And everyone had the belief that the boys would do it, the boys would do it. And eventually, by God's grace was there, and (Mohit) Ulva hit that final shot, and everything went in India's favour," said Aaryavir.The tournament turned out to be a memorable one for Sehwag, who was named Player of the Tournament after scoring 361 runs in five matches at an average of 90.25. His tally included a century and three fifties, while his 16 sixes were the most by any batter in the competition. He also struck half-centuries in both the semifinal and final.However, Sehwag insisted that winning the trophy had been his priority when he arrived for the tournament, rather than focusing on personal milestones."So there were a lot of learnings, a lot of memories, and hopefully I will carry them forward," he said.‘The atmosphere was very tense’: Lakshya on final's pressureFor captain Raichandani, the final was the culmination of an emotional campaign that had tested the team's temperament as much as its cricketing ability."It was an emotional roller coaster. That is right, everyone was very tense, the atmosphere was very tense, and everyone had the belief that the boys will do it, and they did it, hopefully. There were a lot of takeaways, and how to handle your emotion in such a pressure game, how to handle the pressure, how to keep calm, and what to say, when to say to players," he added.Raichandani had also experienced a significant turnaround with the bat. After managing just 70 runs across his first three innings, he produced a superb 93 in the semifinal before scoring 80 off 101 balls in the final. He finished the tournament with 243 runs in five matches at an average of 60.75, including three half-centuries.The final itself had swung repeatedly. Pakistan, opting to bat first, posted 337/9, powered by Usman Khan's 107 off 111 balls, Abdul Qadir's 80 off 54 and Farhan Yousaf's 63 off 60.India's response began positively, with Raichandani and Sehwag putting together a 95-run opening stand. But Pakistan's bowlers fought back, leaving India precariously placed at 252/8 and turning the chase into a test of nerves.Manal Chauhan's 47 off 32 balls and a crucial 67-run partnership with Ulva kept India's hopes alive. After Manal's dismissal, Ulva took responsibility for the finish, smashing an unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls, while Chigurupati Venkata remained unbeaten on 11 to provide valuable support.With India needing to navigate the final moments of a tense chase, Ulva found the boundary off the last ball to complete the victory. For Sehwag, Raichandani and the rest of the squad, it was the payoff for a campaign built on belief, resilience and the ability to handle pressure when the stakes were highest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: With the limited-overs leg of India's ongoing tour of New Zealand completed, attention now turns to the two-match Test series, which begins on Thursday, November 19. The opening encounter will be played at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, with the visitors facing a challenging task against a side that has enjoyed considerable success against them in recent years.New Zealand, currently sitting at the top of the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 points table, have won their last three Tests against India, including matches played both at home and away. Led by Tom Latham, the hosts will be looking to extend their winning streak to five matches.The Kiwis have opted for a full-strength squad for the home series. India, meanwhile, have limited experience of playing Test cricket in New Zealand, with only three members of their 16-player squad having previously featured in Tests in the country.However, most of India's Test regulars, barring Shubman Gill and Gurnoor Brar, recently represented India A in a three-match unofficial Test series against New Zealand A. The matches provided the visitors with an opportunity to acclimatise to local conditions ahead of the important two-Test assignment.As India prepare for another challenging tour, a look at their historical record in New Zealand reveals a mixed history, with only two series victories in 10 visits and five wins across 25 Test matches.India's Test series record in New ZealandIndia first toured New Zealand for a Test series in February-March 1968, under the captaincy of Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi. The visitors made an impressive start to their overseas campaign, winning three of the four matches to register a 3-1 series triumph.However, their next series victory in New Zealand took another 41 years to arrive. India finally broke the drought in 2009 under MS Dhoni, securing a 1-0 win in a three-match series.In the intervening years, India endured several difficult tours. Two series ended in draws, while New Zealand came out on top in six contests, including the last two bilateral Test series played in the country.The most recent visit, in February-March 2020, was particularly disappointing for India, who suffered a 2-0 whitewash.India's Test series results in New ZealandSeasonMatchesScorelineWinnerIndia captain1968 (February-March)43-1IndiaMansoor Ali Khan Pataudi1976 (January-February)31-1DrawBishan Singh Bedi (2), Sunil Gavaskar (1)1981 (February-March)31-0New ZealandSunil Gavaskar1990 (February)31-0New ZealandMohammad Azharuddin1994 (March)10-0DrawMohammad Azharuddin1998-99 (December-January)21-0New ZealandMohammad Azharuddin2002 (December)22-0New ZealandSourav Ganguly2009 (March-April)31-0IndiaMS Dhoni (2), Virender Sehwag (1)2014 (February)21-0New ZealandMS Dhoni2020 (February-March)22-0New ZealandVirat KohliIndia's Test match record in New ZealandIndia's overall numbers in New Zealand underline how difficult the conditions have been for visiting teams from the subcontinent. articles.body: Bengal recorded a convincing 85-run victory against Chandigarh to get back on the winning ways in their second Group ‘A’ match of the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 meet at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on Monday.While pacer Mukesh Kumar made amends for leaking runs in the first match against Karnataka, Karan Lal came good with both bat and ball to make a difference.Put into bat after losing the toss, Bengal made a fluent start with wicketkeeper-batter Abishek Porel going on the onslaught from the word go. The left-hander hit Sandeep Sharma for a six and a four in the very first over and repeated the same in the second over off Jagjit Singh. Lal too hit two fours and one six before falling for 21. Bengal suffered a minor jolt as from 74 for no loss in the sixth over, they were reduced to 84/3 by the ninth over losing Lal, Porel and Sudip Gharami in quick succession.Skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran and Shakib Gandhi then steadied the ship with a 43-run fourth-wicket stand. Although the Bengal middle-order batters failed to get the boundaries often, they kept the scoreboard moving by rotating the strike well that helped them finish at 200 for seven.Bengal pacers Mukesh and Mohammed Shami struck early as Chandigarh lost skipper Manan Vohra and Shivam Bhambri in consecutive overs. Mukesh was at it again claiming Chiragvir Dhindsa in his second over to finish his first spell at 2-0-6-2.The spinners then came into play with Lal getting Aarush Bhandari and Arjun Azad in his first and second overs, while Pradipta Pramanik having Sanyam Saini in his second over. Lal then bowled Bhagmender Lather in his last over to finish with 3-34 in his four overs.Mukesh returned to wrap up the Chandigarh innings having Jagjit Singh caught by Easwaran and then got Rohit Dhanda caught behind in the first over of his second spell to return with 4-9 in 2.5 overs, as Chandigarh were bowled out for mere 115 runs in 15.5 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
